came upon a Dicks sporting goods sale event ,  so ordered three products , got email with order # but I didn't feel right about it after the fact so called Dicks Sporting Goods and found out it is a scam using their name !! so locked all my credit cards and contacted my bank , one charge for 35.99 for one coat was on my debit card charge posted yesterday , but when I looked at bank sight again tonight it was gone , not sure what is going on with that so sent text to bank stating what happened , so not sure if I lost money or not but other transaction was not on bank sight or on any of my credit cards so hope not out of my money !! learned my lesson for sure

I entered a contract with Cloudgain for 1 year in October 2025. I would supposedly get numerous patient referrals. Did not get hardly any referrals, meaning not even enough to pay for the service. Then without any notification; Coudgain took $2910.18 out of my bank account. As soon as I noticed I called Cloudgain after searching for the number. Received a recording say they were away from their desk and would call back. Cloudgain (Shawn) called back and I told him I wanted my money returned period. I said there is nothing to discuss I do not want the service and I want my money back. The next day same thing except He would talk to the billing department. Over a week now no call back. I have called daily getting the same answering machine message they are away from my desk right now but will return your call. It is wrong to take money out of anyone's account without notifying them first. Shawn stated it is in the contract autorenewal. Even then I should have been notified 1st. This is just plain theft.

I got a call from someone saying they were from a ""Legal Department"" (didn't give a agency or company name) And they had legal documents that needed deliver and wanted me to verify my address. (they had my correct address but I didn't verify it with them). I told her that this was a spam phone call and she told me they would use this recording in court and she hung up.

I was checking my bank statement and found several fraudulent charges from a business called www.mossbrady.com. I had never heard of them, never ordered their services. I called and emailed them and never got any response. (I reported it to my bank and am getting a new debit card). I have no idea how they got my bank information, these were several recurring charges from them, each at $49.99 and totaling $499.91.

The "company" popped up as an ad on my phone. Once I clicked on it, it then attempted to take my PayPal information. I never signed up for an account. Each day since, the company is attempting to charge my credit card $29.90 per day. My CC company is declining it. I tried emailing the support@uryogajourney.com to stop this charge attempt, and the email address is getting sent back and is not a real email account.

On July 31, 2026 I thought was helping a friend who asked for me to send the money thru ***** to a recruiter to process paperwork to be able to leave the military early.  Person tried to say the money was never received. Both my bank and ***** refuse to pay the money back. This money was my 401k loan and now I am paying for a loan on money that i did not receive. The person tried to say it was the money he deposited into my bank. Bank informed me they declined that transaction cause it was coming from out of state.

I found a website PROMOTED BY GOOGLE! called Lolli & Lace that had a costume my 6yo wanted for Halloween. They said 5 to 7 business days and I ordered on Oct 9th. By the 27th I emailed them to ask where my package was. I received a generic “thanks for you order, it’s on the way response” to which I sent back demanding my items arrive within 48 hours or I would take action. The site has since been shut down and there is no way to contact them with many other consumers making the same claims. I’ve contacted my bank to try to get a refund. But I also think that these sites should not be promoted by other companies if they have not done proper investigation into the legitimacy of the companies.
